details 7000, avenue du Parc, bureau 312, Montreal QC H3N 1X1 514-340-9019 Contacts (1)
LAURENCE LESER Director 514-340-9019 Communicate with this contact Mission Founded in
1976, the Spina Bifida Association and Hydrocephalus of Quebec (ASBHQ)'s mission is to improve
the quality of life of its members and those whose lives are affected by spina bifida. This is our
reason for being, and we we are at your disposal! Description The ASBHQ is concerned with
playing a vital role with affected people and their families. Whether after the announcement of the
diagnosis of spina bifida, during pregnancy, or when an adult with spina bifida wonders about As his
case evolves, the ASBHQ becomes an important resource. We understand the anxiety, confusion
and worry experienced by those affected and their families. We work with heart in order to provide
them with all the information available so that they can make the choices that are required in their
individual case. Here is a general overview of the ASBHQ mandate. Support and encourage
research to determine the causes of spina bifida, enable improvement of treatments and prevention
techniques. Disseminate information about spina bifida and to hydrocephalus in his publication Le
Spinnaker. Organize information sessions and training, ensure the production of documentation,
promotional tours and awareness across Quebec. See to the development of services that meet the
needs of people with spina bifida and their families. Provide a consultation and references. Raise
awareness among the population of Quebec about spina bifida and prevention measures. Assume
a role of leadership and cohesion with regional associations to implement common ideas and
experiences across Quebec. Prepare and monitor the dissemination of the advertising for the
various media, so that the ASBHQ message is standardized and in accordance with policies
already established. Play a political role with government authorities and other decision-making
powers, for any questions concerning the integration of people with impairment, particularly people
with spina bifida and hydrocephalus. Bring a support for regional associations by offering them
expertise and planning tools, organization, promotion, etc. The ASBHQ attaches major importance
to consultation and partnership with other organizations in the community, public, or parapublic
sectors, in order to better develop services that will meet the needs of its members. His partners or
life members are the Constance-Lethbridge Rehabilitation Center (CRCL), the Physical Impairment
Rehabilitation Institute of Quebec (IRDPQ), the Rehabilitation Center Chaudière-Appalaches
(CRDP-CA) and the Shriners Hospital for Children. We actively collaborate with the following
organizations, on issues of common interest: education, integration, school adaptation, integration
into daycare, adapted transportation, equity, family policy, employment, etc. : The Office for
Disabled Persons of Quebec (OPHQ), the Confederation of organizations of disabled people in
Quebec (COPHAN), the Adaptation Committee of the workforce (CAMO) for disabled people and
the Quebec Student Association with disabilities in postsecondary education (AQEIPS).

confidentiality in all our interactions. Services offered Emotional and psychological support for
patients and their families Reliable information on cancer types, treatments and community
resources Complementary therapies and free practical resources Center of Resources The
CanSupport Des Cèdres Resource Center is a welcoming space that provides health information to

books on general health and cancer Wig and head covering loan program for cancer patients For
more information about our services and how to benefit from our support, do not hesitate to contact

Organization 60: Project 10 URL: https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/projet10/ Website:
https://p10.qc.ca/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 10138 Rue
Lajeunesse, Montréal QC H3L 2E2 514 989-0001 Opening hours SCHEDULE Check the schedule
on our website. Networks social Mission Project 10 works to promote the personal, social, sexual
and mental well-being of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, two-spirit, intersex and other youth
and adults questions aged between 14 and 25. Description INDIVIDUAL MEETING & SUPPORT
Project 10 offers individual intervention sessions for young people and/or their families to discuss
topics related to sexual orientation and/or gender identity. In addition of these individual meetings,
we also offer support services for users of Project 10. In the past, we have accompanied people to
appointments medical services, including HIV testing, at social assistance offices, interviews for
housing cooperatives, other community organizations, centers accommodation, as well as
appearances at court. GROUP (DROP-IN) Project 10 has a group regular bilingual on Thursday
evening for young people aged 14 to 25 and Tuesday evening for teenagers (14 to 17). The group
is open and semi-structured, led by employees and interns. The content of the group is largely
decided by young people. You are in charge of the activities! Once a month, a mix of ideas is
carried out to decide on the schedule for the next month. Activities favorites of the group included
our spring barbecue and our very special P10 idol party! DEFENSE OF RIGHTS Project 10 workers
and interns campaign for several participants of Project 10, so that they can achieve their goals,
whether it is finding a affordable apartment, find a job, change the name and gender designated to
them on the official identity papers, access to sex reassignment surgeries, obtain status of refugee,
stay out of prison, complete complaint documents for experienced discrimination, and even more.
KIOSKS AND WORKSHOPS We offer information workshops for young people, teachers and
social workers. We offer a workshop adapted to the needs of people concerned, but we try to
concentrate on activities which aim to share information and resources, undo prejudices and invite
discussion and to questions about sexual orientation and gender identity. We also have kiosks in
schools and in community events to increase our visibility and share information. To obtain a
workshop or kiosk, call the helpline (514 989 4585) or send a message to questions@p10.qc.ca
TRANS HEALTH At Projet 10, we work hard to find doctors and other health professionals who are
qualified and knowledgeable to work with trans youth in an open and non-judgmental way. To this
end, we maintain a database of physicists, therapists, etc. for Trans Health. In this way, we can
refer our participants to these health specialists. Recently, the work team of Project 10 has been an
active member of a Trans Health Network to improve access for trans people to health services.

Organization 64: Canadian Psychoanalytic Society URL:

chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges, Montreal QC H3S 2C1 514 738-6105 Opening hours SCHEDULE
Monday to Friday Mission La Canadian Psychoanalytic Society is committed to providing
comprehensive training in psychoanalysis and to provide intensive psychotherapy services to
promote personal development and resolution of unsatisfactory life patterns. Support individuals in
a process of deep transformation, exploring personal and interpersonal experiences to improve
mental health and well-being. Description The Canadian Psychoanalytic Society (SCP)! Since
1957, the SCP has offered psychoanalysis services in Canada. As an institute dynamic and
progressive, we are committed to providing psychoanalytic training comprehensive for mental
health professionals of all levels. Psychoanalysis in Canada We practice an intensive form of
psychotherapy that promotes personal development and resolving unsatisfactory or painful life
patterns. Our members work closely collaboration with individuals to improve their mental health by
examining meticulously personal and interpersonal experiences, the interaction between the past
and the present, the connection between body and mind, and the dynamic between fantasy and
reality. Process psychoanalytic The process requires the establishment of a relationship of trust
with the analyst, in complete confidentiality. Sessions generally take place 3 to 4 times a week, thus
favoring the emergence of the analysand’s dilemmas and traumas. Private listening of the analyst
allows us to explore the experience of the analysand through his emotional reactions, his thoughts,
memories, fantasies, dreams, images and bodily sensations. Training and members Our members
are psychoanalysts, members of the Association international psychoanalytic (API). We offer the
best training in psychoanalysis in the Canada, recognized for its rigor by the IPA. CPS Ottawa
